title.narrative: IPAS - Building Commitment and Capacity for Sustainable Abortion Care in DRC
IPAS - Engagemang och kapacitet för säker abortvård i DRK

description.narrative:
Ipas DRC samarbetar med partners för att se till att kvinnor och flickor i Demokratiska republiken Kongo (DRK) kan få tillgång till säker abortvård och utöva sina mänskliga rättigheter till hälsa och autonomi.
Denna insats syftar till att stärka UNFPA: s kapacitet att leverera de resultat som anges i organisationens landprogram för DRK under perioden 2020–2023.
I DRK är alla indikatorer som rör kvinnors sexuella och reproduktiva hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) oroande, framför allt är den knappa tillgången till preventivmedel och det höga antalet ungdomsgraviditeter alarmerande. Dessutom är den övergripande policymiljön när det gäller SRHR och befolkningsdynamik inte anpassad till landets utmaningar. UNFPA är en nyckelaktör i DRK, vars starka insatser inom ramen för dess globala mandat behövs för att stödja både beslutsfattare, genomförande aktörer på internationell och nationell nivå, och kunna nå ut till olika målgrupper som kvinnor, ungdomar, vårdgivare och institutioner.
Detta institutionella stöd till UNFPA ger dem flexibilitet, frihet och medel för att positionera sig och ge stöd till aktörer inom SRHR och relaterade frågor i landet.

Ipas DRC works with partners to ensure that women and girls in the DRC can access safe abortion care, exercising their human right to health and autonomy. This project aims at providing government stakeholders and selected NGOs, including community organizations and youth-serving, youth-led groups, improved knowledge of the Maputo Protocol and ensuring that they have strengthened capacity and commitment to support women’s rights to broader reproductive health services, including abortion. Key government stakeholders, including the Ministry of Public Health and the Ministry of Gender will the champion national ownership and integration of the Maputo Protocol. This project aligns closely with Sweden’s groundbreaking feminist foreign policy, interest in addressing unsafe abortion’s impact on maternal mortality, and commitment to sustainable health systems that offer equal access to high-quality care.

The project is expected to contribute to expanded access to reproductive health care and rights, including safe abortion, in the DRC. The goal is to strengthen national ownership and the long-term sustainability of reproductive health care, including abortion care in the DRC. The programme goal will be achieved by contributing to an enabling environment through the domestication of the Maputo Protocol and the finalization of standard and guidelines development for safe abortion by the Ministry of Public Health—thus leading to an improvement in comprehensive abortion care access in the country. This process will involve mobilization of stakeholders in the civil society, including youth associations and professional bodies (e.g. midwives association) capable of promoting the rights perspective in the demand and supply sides of vital reproductive health services.

The annual report for 2024 is expected on the 31st July, 2025 and as such the results from the final report 20212023, and MTR that (analysed in April of 2024) is still valid.
1. Secured multiministerial engagement (Gender, Health, Human Rights, Youth) Supported development of DRCs first Comprehensive Abortion Care (CAC) Standards & Guidelines, a major milestone in Francophone Africa. Backed by a Constitutional Court decision affirming the Maputo Protocols supremacy.
2. Justice System Strengthening Trained 3,128 magistrates and judges using a Maputo Protocol Training Guide. Established a national pool of 400 trained magistrates as abortion focal points. Engaged female lawyers to defend prosecuted womenen hancing access to legal protection.
3. Community Engagement & Social Norm Change Partnered with 75 youth and women led organizations worked with Men to tackle stigma. Reached 2.4 million people with accurate SRHR info ~17,000 participated in positive masculinity dialogues. Normalized abortion discourse via social media events and national dialogues featuring government and civil society.
4. Health System Strengthening: Collaborated with 8 provincial health authorities. Trained 278 health providers and created a national pool of CAC master trainers. Activated 118 health facilities to offer safe abortion services. Integrated abortion indicators into DHIS2 and medical school curricula (University of Kinshasa). Set up Centers of Excellence for highquality care and provider training.
5. Service Delivery Outcomes. 22,387 women and girls accessed safe abortion services across 9 provinces. Impact (estimates): 187,147 unintended pregnancies averted 45,472 unsafe abortions averted 675 maternal deaths averted The MTR had 13 recomendations i.e. i) Maintain momentum & expand to more provinces (ii) Continuity amidst staff turnover in government & judiciary (iii) Followup on 30 partners trained previously (iv)Create community referral pathways through subgrantees (v) Collaborate with SANRU and SCOSAF for midwifery training (vi) National ownership & Maputo Protocol awareness (vii) Translate "strengthen capacity" into service delivery(viii) Increase IEC materials on abortion at CSO and facility levels (ix) Continued awareness & intergenerational dialogue (x) National forum on shared strategy for Maputo Protocol dissemination (xi) Present research results on domestication impact (xii) Improve data collection (DHIS2) on abortion outcomes (xiii) Quarterly Pause & Reflect with partners. Six of the Thirteen recommendations have been adequately addressed in the concept note that was approved and financed in 2025
Momentum and Expansion: Activities planned in North Kivu and Kasai expansion via mobile clinics, subgrants, and COEs. Continuity & Training amidst Staff Turnover: Activity 1.1 plans VCAT and sensitization for new government, legal, and community actors. To be achieved through planned VCAT trainings and sensitization for new government/legal personnel.
Midwifery Training : Integrated in midwife training in Partnership with SCOSAF and PNSR for capacity building under CAC and GBV.
Community Referral Pathways: Developed via community engagement, hotline 122, mobile clinics, and youth champions
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
